Project-Level Predecisional Administrative Review Process
articles.summary: The U.S. Department of Agriculture is issuing a final rule amending its Project-Level Predecisional Administrative Review Process regulations. These regulations establish the process by which the public may file objections seeking administrative review of proposed projects and activities implementing land management plans on national forests and grasslands. The Department is amending these regulations to consolidate and streamline processes, increase efficiency, and better align with the Agency's statutory obligations and recent rescissions and revisions to National Environmental Policy Act regulations.

articles.title: Magnuson-Stevens Act Provisions; Fisheries off West Coast States; Pacific Coast Groundfish Fishery; Pacific Coast Groundfish Fishery Management Plan; Fixed Gear Marking and Entanglement Risk Reduction
articles.summary: This rulemaking implements gear marking requirements and entanglement risk reduction measures for portions of the Pacific coast groundfish fishery. This rulemaking consists of mandatory requirements and voluntary measures. These new requirements and voluntary measures are established pursuant to the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act (Magnuson-Stevens Act). The intent of the gear marking requirements is to increase the likelihood of attributing entanglements to a specific fishery and gear type. The intent of the risk reduction measures is to reduce bycatch by decreasing the likelihood of marine animal entanglements with fishing line.

articles.title: Fisheries of the Northeastern United States; Summer Flounder Fishery; 2026 Commercial Quota Harvested for the State of Maine
articles.summary: NMFS announces that the 2026 summer flounder commercial quota allocated to the State of Maine has been harvested. Vessels issued a commercial Federal fisheries permit for the summer flounder fishery may not land summer flounder in Maine for the remainder of calendar year 2026, unless additional quota becomes available through a transfer from another state. Regulations governing the summer flounder fishery require publication of this notification to advise Maine that the quota has been harvested, and to advise vessel permit holders and dealer permit holders that no Federal commercial quota is available for landing summer flounder in Maine.

articles.summary: NMFS is adjusting the Atlantic bluefin tuna (BFT) General category October through November 2026 time period subquota by transferring 70.2 metric tons (mt) of quota from the Reserve category. Simultaneously, NMFS is adding 16.7 mt of subquota remaining from the June through August time period to the General category October through November time period. This action results in a total adjusted General category October through November time period subquota of 192.9 mt and an adjusted Reserve category of 42 mt. This action would affect Atlantic Tunas General category (commercial) permitted vessels and Highly Migratory Species (HMS) Charter/Headboat permitted vessels with a commercial sale endorsement when fishing commercially for BFT.

articles.content: Tsakos returns to containership contracting in China - Splash247 Hengli Shipbuilding Greek shipping group Tsakos has returned to the containership newbuilding market, emerging behind an order for two 3,200 teu vessels at China’s Hengli Heavy Industries. The pair appear in the Athens-based owner’s latest fleet register, with both scheduled for delivery in the fourth quarter of 2028. Both will be scrubber-fitted and equipped with alternative maritime power systems, allowing them to connect to shore-side electricity while alongside. Shipping database records point to contracts signed in September, although Alphaliner said the exact timing remains unclear and that the orders could have been concluded in August or September. Market sources put the ships at around $48m each, depending on final specification, implying a combined investment of about $96m. Neither Tsakos nor Hengli has disclosed pricing. Charter arrangements are also unknown. Alphaliner noted that Tsakos has typically backed containership newbuildings with forward employment, but there is no indication yet whether the Hengli pair have already been fixed. The deal marks Tsakos’ first return to boxship contracting since 2022, when the group booked a series of approximately 2,800 teu vessels at HD Hyundai Mipo in South Korea. articles.content: Falklands offshore development faces new international legal challenge - Splash247 Falkland Islands Govt The dispute over offshore oil development around the Falkland Islands has escalated, with Argentina seeking emergency measures from an international maritime tribunal while the UK moves to protect companies involved in economic activity linked to the islands. Argentina filed a request with the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea (ITLOS), seeking provisional measures to prevent the UK from authorising hydrocarbon exploitation on the North Falkland Basin continental shelf. The filing forms part of an arbitration Buenos Aires launched against the UK under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea. Argentina argues that continued oil development could undermine its claimed sovereign rights and, while the dispute remains unresolved, risk serious harm to the marine environment. “The Argentine Republic reaffirms, once again, its legitimate and imprescriptible sovereign rights over the Malvinas Islands, South Georgia, and the South Sandwich Islands and the surrounding maritime areas. By history and by right: the Falkland Islands are Argentine,” the government said in its statement. London responded immediately with plans to use its Protection of Trading Interests legislation to shield UK companies and individuals from Argentine measures targeting activity around the Falklands. articles.content: Hurricane Isaias: Category 3 Threat to Gulf & Supply Chain - FreightWaves Hurricane Isaias is intensifying in the Gulf, threatening to become a Category 3 storm and unleash significant damage across the Southeast. We break down the storm’s projected path, its potential impact on critical infrastructure like refineries and ports, and what freight and logistics operators can expect for trucking capacity and diesel prices. Stay ahead of the storm’s supply chain disruptions with our full analysis. Hurricane Isaias, currently a Category 1 storm, is forecast to strengthen to a Category 2 by Wednesday and potentially reach Category 3 with winds of up to 100 miles per hour before making landfall Friday around 2 p.m., according to a FreightWaves Sonar analysis. The storm’s projected path stretches from just east of Houston across to the Florida Panhandle, encompassing major freight corridors and energy infrastructure in the Gulf Coast region. The most consequential supply chain risk lies in the energy sector. Up to six refineries sit in the storm’s path, and Gulf State refineries collectively account for 50% of the nation’s refining capacity — a total of 18.2 million barrels per day. Offshore production operators are already sending home nonessential workers, though output continues normally for now. articles.content: Sanctioned 22-Year-Old Tanker Makes Rare Late-Season Arctic Voyage Oil tanker along Northern Sea Route in July 2025. (Source: Atomflot) Sanctioned 22-Year-Old Tanker Makes Rare Late-Season Arctic Voyage Malte Humpert Total Views: 178 October 7, 2026 A 22-year-old product tanker sanctioned by the European Union is making an unusual late-season voyage along Russia’s Northern Sea Route, highlighting the growing use of older, lower-specification vessels to move petroleum products through the Arctic. The Dakar, a 21,300-dwt oil and chemical products tanker built in 2004, is carrying methyl tert-butyl ether (MTBE), a gasoline additive, and appears to be heading west along Russia’s Arctic coast, according vessel tracking data. The cargo was loaded onto another vessel in China in August before being transferred to Dakar off Yeosu, South Korea, in September. Dakar is not an Arctic-specialist tanker, but vessel data from S&P Global indicates that it does have an ice-class designation. That distinguishes it from non-ice-class tankers, while placing it well below the Arc4 and higher ice-class vessels purpose-built for regular Arctic operations. The distinction is increasingly relevant as Russia’s shadow fleet expands its presence on the Northern Sea Route. Advocacy group Bellona identified 50 shadow-fleet oil tankers on the NSR between the start of the 2026 summer-autumn navigation season and mid-September, compared with 38 during the entire 2025 season. articles.content: Despite new record, Port of LA chief warns of tariff-driven planning risk - FreightWaves The Port of Los Angeles moved 1.42 million TEUs in September, its best single month ever and the highest monthly volume ever recorded by a port in the Western Hemisphere, Executive Director Gene Seroka said this week. He said lower tariff levels, resilient consumer demand, and cargo shifting away from constrained Panama Canal and Suez routes drove the surge. Record quarter September imports totaled 546,000 loaded TEUs, up 19% year over year and 26% above the port’s five-year average. Exports rose 10% to 126,000 loaded TEUs, while the port handled a record 371,000 empty containers as carriers repositioned equipment to Asia. July through September was the port’s strongest quarter on record at nearly 3 million TEUs, and June through September moved nearly 4 million containers. Through September, 2026 volume stood at nearly 8.1 million TEUs, up about 3% from the same period in 2025. Seroka said the port expects October volume of about 900,000 TEUs. He cited typhoon-related schedule disruptions in Asia, cargo “roll pools” before China’s national holiday, and continued holiday-season replenishment as reasons volumes should remain elevated. Trade and sourcing shifts Seroka in a media briefing said Vietnam is now the port’s second-largest trading partner behind China, while Thailand has entered the port’s top five for the first time. articles.content: Mexico truck exports soar 145% as US demand accelerates - FreightWaves Mexican manufacturers produced 15,181 heavy-duty vehicles during September, compared with 6,857 in the same month last year. Exports totaled 12,707 units, up 144.6% from September 2025, marking a significant acceleration in cross-border commercial vehicle shipments, according to figures from Mexico’s National Institute of Statistics and Geography (INEGI) presented by the National Association of Bus, Truck and Tractor-Trailer Producers (ANPACT). The September rebound comes as Mexico’s domestic heavy-duty vehicle market continues to struggle with weak sales, delayed fleet replacement decisions and uncertainty surrounding U.S. trade policies. Rogelio Arzate, executive president of ANPACT, said growing demand from U.S. customers preparing for new emissions standards has been a major factor behind the increase in production and exports. “The reason why production and exports are growing at the levels they are is precisely because the United States, our main trading partner, is currently undergoing this technology shift,” Arzate said during an October news conference. OK SEOUL, Oct. 13 (Yonhap) -- President Lee Jae Myung on Tuesday reaffirmed South Korea's push to develop a new shipping route through the Arctic Ocean, saying it will be pursued in compliance with international norms and sanctions. The president made the pledge at a ceremony celebrating South Korea's successful voyage to Europe through the Arctic Ocean by a container ship, as the country seeks to operate summer-season container shipping services linking Asia and Europe. The PanStar Acro, a South Korean container ship, returned to the southeastern port city of Busan on Sunday after sailing via the Arctic Ocean north of Russia to Britain, the Netherlands and Poland, 50 days after leaving Busan. The pilot voyage marks the first successful trip by a South Korean container vessel via the Arctic Ocean, a route which is riskier due to polar ice, but offers faster shipping than routes via the Suez Canal. Growing international use of the Arctic route has, however, raised concerns that cooperation with Russian entities could undermine international sanctions imposed on Russia over its war with Ukraine. articles.content: Emarat Maritime piles six more tankers onto China orderbook - Splash247 Jiangsu New Hantong Ship Heavy Industry Dubai-based Emarat Maritime has added another six tanker newbuildings to its rapidly expanding fleet, lining up a series of 74,000 dwt LR1 product carriers in China. The company’s own fleet register now lists six LR1 newbuildings, with the first two scheduled for delivery in 2029 and the remaining four in 2030. Shipbuilding database records seen by Splash place the sextet at Jiangsu New Hantong Ship Heavy Industry. No contract price has emerged. Recent comparable Chinese LR1 orders have been running at around $55m per ship. Kriton Lendoudis-led Evalend paid about $220m for four 74,000 dwt ships at Yangzijiang this summer, while Andriaki was linked to 73,500 dwt units at New Times at $55.1m each. On that basis, the Emarat sextet would benchmark at around $330m, although its actual contract terms remain undisclosed. The latest move significantly deepens Emarat’s exposure to the LR1 sector. Its operating fleet currently includes three older ships of roughly the same size — the 2007-built Dubai Diamond and Dubai Gold and the 2005-built Dubai Green. Delivery of the six new ships would therefore triple its LR1 fleet. The deal also takes Emarat’s overall newbuilding pipeline to 22 vessels. articles.content: Sweden frees sanctioned tanker after seven months - Splash247 Swedish Coast Guard Swedish authorities have cleared an EU-sanctioned product tanker to leave the country after nearly seven months at anchor following an investigation into its registration and seaworthiness. The Swedish Transport Agency has lifted an operating ban on the 2007-built, 75,000 dwt Sea Owl I, after confirming that the vessel is now legitimately registered in Equatorial Guinea. The tanker had been detained off Trelleborg since March 12, when Swedish authorities boarded it over concerns about its flag status and documentation. The ship was originally claiming registration in Comoros, which authorities found to be invalid. A subsequent attempt to establish registration under the Cameroon flag also failed verification. The Swedish Transport Agency said it had now received confirmation directly from Equatorial Guinea and had reviewed the certificates and crew documentation required for the vessel to resume operations. The decision removes the Swedish operating prohibition, although the tanker remains subject to EU sanctions. Sweden’s coastguard stressed that the vessel was not suspected of breaching sanctions. Investigations involving two former masters, including allegations concerning false documentation, have been discontinued. Photo courtesy Port of Los Angeles U.S. Container Imports Slow After Stronger-Than-Expected Summer Mike Schuler Total Views: 50 October 8, 2026 U.S. container imports are finally beginning to slow after an unusually long peak shipping season that stretched through the summer and into early fall, according to the latest Global Port Tracker report from the National Retail Federation (NRF) and Hackett Associates. The slowdown comes after months of stronger-than-expected cargo volumes at major U.S. ports, as retailers continued bringing in merchandise despite tariffs, inflation and higher transportation costs. Ports covered by Global Port Tracker handled 2.3 million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs) in August, up 0.4% from July but down 0.7% from a year earlier. The ratio of unfilled orders to shipments rose to 6.87 from 6.81. Census does not adjust the figures for inflation. Orders for motor vehicle bodies, parts and trailers rose 0.8%. Machinery orders rose 1.1%. Nondefense capital goods orders excluding aircraft rose 1.6%. Durable goods orders fell 0.1%, with transportation equipment down 0.7% and nondefense aircraft and parts down 4.3%. articles.content: AI gold rush transforms trans-Pacific trade and logistics - FreightWaves The artificial intelligence infrastructure boom is creating significant new trade flows and opportunities for third-party logistics providers and carriers. Freight transportation companies are rapidly scaling up capabilities, especially to support semiconductor supply chains in Asia, the epicenter for production and distribution of advanced chips used to power AI applications, data centers, connected devices and next-generation vehicles. Two reports issued on Wednesday show how AI-related goods such as semiconductors and data-transmission equipment have become a major driver of international trade growth, spawning increasingly complex regional and global supply chains that depend on speed, visibility, cross-border expertise and resilience. Unlike traditional consumer electronics, AI infrastructure requires the coordinated movement, including customs clearance and storage, of oversized, high-value and highly sensitive equipment from manufacturers across Asia to hyperscale data centers under construction around the world. Semiconductors, data transmission equipment and data center hardware accounted for 42% of all goods trade growth in 2025, and that share rose to about 76% during the first quarter, according to an annual report on globalization trends by the New York University Stern School of Business, and commissioned by DHL Group. Currently, South Korea prohibits exports of strategic items to Russia and subjects an additional 1,402 non-strategic items that could potentially be used for military purposes to case-by-case export authorization, according to the ministry. (c) REUTERS/Edgard Garrido Mexican Auto Exports Slump in September as US Tariffs Take Toll Reuters Total Views: 116 October 8, 2026 By Sarah Morland MEXICO CITY, Oct 8 (Reuters) – Mexico’s auto exports posted their biggest slump so far this year, data from statistics office INEGI showed on Wednesday, a decline analysts attributed to tariff policies from the US, the biggest market for the Latin American country’s top industrial sector. Mexico auto exports fell 12% in September compared to a year earlier, the steepest decline since December 2025, while monthly output slumped 15%. Domestic sales, however, increased 8%, helping buffer the pain for the key manufacturing industry. The data comes as government officials review the US-Mexico-Canada free trade pact, but even with talks continuing, Mexican cars still face tariffs of 25%. Mexican officials estimate that complying with rules that stipulate using North American-sourced parts brings the burden down to 10% to 12%. articles.title: China nominates Song Li for WHO chief as agency faces funding shake-up from US exit
articles.summary:
China has nominated health official Song Li to run for director general of the World Health Organization, the foreign ministry confirmed on Thursday.

articles.content: Almi Marine founder Evgenia Daskalopoulou dies - Splash247 Almi Marine Management Greek shipowner Evgenia Daskalopoulou, founder and president of dry bulk outfit Almi Marine Management, has died. Almi announced her death on Wednesday, saying she passed away surrounded by her family. Daskalopoulou was born in 1958 and founded the Athens-based company in 1992. She built Almi from a small dry bulk operation into a modern supramax and ultramax owner and manager. Greek shipping records show the company started out with two 1970-built handysize bulkers. “More than that, she shaped its character,” Almi said in announcing her death, highlighting her emphasis on integrity and respect for staff both ashore and at sea. The company said operations would continue as normal and that the Daskalopoulou family and management team remained committed to carrying on the business. Almi currently manages six bulkers totalling 365,140 dwt — three supramaxes and three 64,000 dwt ultramaxes. Its fleet includes the 2024-built Mea Mare, Spike and Subra, alongside the older Altus, Anima and Sole. The company has also been building up its future fleet. In February, Almi signed for two 64,000 dwt ultramaxes at Nantong COSCO KHI Ship Engineering, or NACKS, for delivery in the second quarter of 2029. OK SEOUL, Oct. 12 (Yonhap) -- The European Union (EU) on Monday added three individuals and four entities to its sanctions list targeting North Korea over its nuclear and missile programs and ties with Russia. "The Council today adopted additional restrictive measures against three individuals and four entities under its autonomous sanctions list on the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK)," the European Council said in a statement. The DPRK is the acronym of North Korea's official name. The council said the individuals and entities were responsible for supporting, promoting or facilitating activities contributing to North Korea's nuclear weapons, ballistic missile and other weapons of mass destruction programs, as well as for violating and evading United Nations sanctions. articles.content: Sweden Releases Sanctioned Russian Shadow Fleet Tanker After Seven-Month Detention The sanctioned tanker Sea Owl 1 underway at sea. Swedish authorities have cleared the vessel to leave Sweden after a nearly seven-month detention over registration and documentation irregularities. Photo: Swedish Coast Guard (Kustbevakningen). Sweden Releases Sanctioned Russian Shadow Fleet Tanker After Seven-Month Detention Mike Schuler Total Views: 318 October 12, 2026 Swedish authorities have cleared the sanctioned tanker Sea Owl 1 to leave the country after nearly seven months at anchor, following confirmation that the vessel is now legitimately registered under the flag of Equatorial Guinea. The Swedish Transport Agency announced Monday that it had lifted an operating ban imposed on the tanker in March over irregularities involving its flag registration and documentation. The vessel has remained anchored off Trelleborg, on Sweden’s southern coast, since authorities boarded it on March 12 amid concerns over its seaworthiness and registration status. According to the Swedish Coast Guard, the tanker was initially found to be falsely flying the flag of Comoros. An attempt to reflag the vessel to Cameroon in May also proved invalid, leaving the ship effectively without a recognized flag state. The Swedish Transport Agency said it has now received direct confirmation from Equatorial Guinea that the tanker is properly registered. articles.content: OOCL revenue up 45.1% on trans-Pacific surge - FreightWaves Orient Overseas Container Line reported a 45.1% year-over-year increase in third-quarter liner revenue to $3.28 billion, as higher revenue per container and increased cargo volumes drove gains across all four of its reported trade regions. OOCL handled 2.12 million twenty-foot equivalent units in the quarter ended Sept. 30, up 9% from a year earlier, according to an Oct. 9 operational update from parent Orient Overseas (International) Ltd., itself majority-owned by China’s Cosco Shipping Holdings. Average liner revenue per TEU increased 33.1%. Cargo growth outpaced a 3.6% increase in loadable capacity. OOIL reported that the overall load factor increased 4.2% compared with the third quarter of 2025. Trans-Pacific leads revenue growth The trans-Pacific trade delivered the largest revenue increase among OOCL’s reported regions. Revenue rose 71.8% to $1.44 billion, while container volumes increased 13.1% to 595,139 TEUs. That compared with revenue of $837.9 million and volumes of 526,032 TEUs in the same quarter last year. Asia-Europe recorded the fastest volume growth, with liftings rising 15.4% to 399,162 TEUs. Revenue on the trade increased 45% to $695.8 million. Intra-Asia and Australasia remained OOCL’s largest region by container volume, handling 981,336 TEUs, up 4.6%. Revenue increased 23.7% to $947.6 million. articles.title: A Virtual Compliance Department for Every Fleet
articles.summary:
Dotra Compliance, an AI-driven platform built to serve as a carrier's "virtual compliance department," is helping small and midsize carriers close the gap between regulatory volume and in-house resources. Co-founder David Vincent explains why, after a Supreme Court ruling reshaped broker liability, a clean compliance record has become as important to winning freight as avoiding fines.
The post A Virtual Compliance Department for Every Fleet appeared first on FreightWaves.
articles.content: A Virtual Compliance Department for Every Fleet - FreightWaves Ask carriers what’s changed about trucking compliance lately, and you’ll likely hear about the accumulation of new rules that change faster than most back offices can absorb them. David Vincent has had a front-row seat to that accumulation. He’s co-founder of Visionary Ventures, the technology company that built and operates Dotra Compliance, a platform designed to serve as what Vincent calls a virtual compliance department. FreightWaves sat down with Vincent to talk through where carriers are losing ground and where a software layer can realistically help. He laid out a picture of an industry squeezed from multiple directions at once, including a faster enforcement, a Supreme Court ruling that rewrote how brokers vet carriers, and a volume of paperwork that outpaces small compliance departments. The current compliance environment, Vincent says, feels more difficult than it used to because it is. Carriers have been dealt a stretch of regulatory change that would challenge any safety department. “In the last 18 months alone, carriers have absorbed English proficiency becoming an out-of-service violation, revoked ELDs, a non-domiciled CDL crackdown, a new FMCSA registration system and a Supreme Court ruling that changed how brokers choose carriers,” Vincent said. The European Union imported a record 12.18 million metric tons of liquefied natural gas from Russia’s Yamal Arctic project in the first nine months of 2026, paying an estimated €7.88 billion, according to an analysis by German environmental group Urgewald. Shipments rose 9.5% compared with the same period last year, even as Yamal’s worldwide deliveries fell 1.3%. Europe received 167 cargoes, accounting for 85% of the project’s recorded deliveries by volume, according to Urgewald’s analysis of Kpler shipping data. The figures highlight Europe’s continuing importance to Russia’s Arctic gas trade despite the EU’s planned phaseout of Russian LNG imports. The bloc’s estimated bill included €2.88 billion in the first quarter, €3.08 billion in the second and €1.92 billion in the third. Third-quarter deliveries fell 13.6% year-over-year to 2.21 million tons. September shipments, however, reached 792,440 tons, slightly above the same month last year, with an estimated value of €818 million. articles.content: Black Sea grain exports crater amid widening maritime war - Splash247 Ambrey Black Sea wheat exports are plunging at the height of the traditional shipping season as escalating attacks on commercial vessels and port infrastructure leave both Russia and Ukraine struggling to get their harvests to international markets. Fresh vessel-tracking data compiled by AXSMarine and published by Greek shipbroker Ursa show wheat loadings across the Black Sea slumped to just 1.6m tonnes in September, 77.8% below the 7.3m tonnes recorded in the same month last year. September volumes were also down 45.6% from August, with shipments falling to their lowest September level since 2017. The collapse is particularly striking given that August and September are normally among the busiest months for Black Sea grain exports as the new harvest comes to market. Across the first nine months of 2026, Black Sea wheat loadings reached 36.3m tonnes, down 12.2% year-on-year and the second-lowest January-to-September total since 2017. The deterioration comes as the maritime war spreads well beyond the immediate approaches to Russian and Ukrainian ports, increasingly threatening alternative grain export corridors. Earlier this week, the Turkish-owned general cargo ship Royad Mammadov, carrying corn from Ukraine’s Danube port of Izmail to Italy, sank following a drone attack in Romania’s exclusive economic zone, killing two seafarers. articles.content: Trøim-backed Bruton opens review amid VLCC sale talk - Splash247 Nor-Shipping Tor Olav Trøim-backed VLCC owner Bruton has launched a strategic review after market speculation over a potential transaction, with International Seaways linked by shipbroking sources to the purchase of at least two of its remaining newbuildings. The Oslo-listed company acknowledged the speculation on Thursday, saying it had started a review aimed at maximising shareholder value. Bruton declined to identify any potential counterparties or elaborate on what form a transaction could take, stressing that there was no certainty a deal would materialise. Market talk has International Seaways negotiating for at least two ships, with the most obvious candidates being the 300,000 dwt Mount Frontier and Mount Summit under construction at New Times Shipyard. The vessels are due in August and October 2027 and, unlike Bruton’s first two VLCCs, have yet to secure employment. Bruton’s latest fleet list shows both without charter coverage. Brokers have circulated numbers north of $200m apiece for the pair. Neither Bruton nor International Seaways has confirmed negotiations or pricing. Bruton’s own investor material lists the yard price of Mount Frontier and Mount Summit at about $117m each. The higher $134m figure attached to the programme applies to the first two LNG dual-fuel ships, Mount Vision and Mount Horizon, rather than the 2027 pair.
